United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Promoting lifelong learning skills development for individuals, the economy and society through TVET

description.narrative:
The world is undergoing profound and interconnected transformations that are reshaping how people learn, work and participate in society. Rapid technological change, including the growing influence of artificial intelligence and digital technologies, the transition towards greener and more sustainable economies, demographic shifts, changing labour markets and persistent social inequalities are creating both new opportunities and significant challenges for individuals, communities and countries. At the same time, many education and training systems struggle to keep pace with these changes, while millions of young people and adults continue to face barriers in accessing relevant learning opportunities and acquiring the skills needed for employment, entrepreneurship, active citizenship and lifelong personal development.
In this context, UNESCO will support Member States in strengthening skills development systems that enable all learners to acquire, update and expand their knowledge, skills and competencies throughout life. Guided by a lifelong learning and rights-based approach, the project seeks to ensure that youth and adults have access to inclusive, equitable and quality learning opportunities that respond to their aspirations, the needs of labour markets and the broader demands of sustainable and peaceful societies. Particular attention will be given to women and girls, vulnerable and marginalized populations, countries in Africa, and Small Island Developing States.
The project aims to strengthen national capacities to design and implement policies, strategies and programmes that improve access to skills development, promote lifelong learning opportunities and support successful transitions between learning and work. It will contribute to helping countries develop more resilient, inclusive and future-oriented systems that equip learners with the skills needed to thrive in rapidly changing economic, social and environmental contexts. The project will also support efforts to align skills development with national development priorities, including digital transformation, climate action, social inclusion and economic diversification.
To achieve these objectives, UNESCO will work with governments, education and training institutions, employers, workers’ organizations, development partners and other stakeholders through three complementary areas of action. First, the project will generate evidence, research and policy guidance to strengthen decision-making and support reforms. This will include analytical studies, policy reviews, labour market and skills analyses, data collection and monitoring activities, as well as the development of practical guidance and tools for policymakers and practitioners. Particular attention will be given to identifying emerging skills needs, improving the understanding of labour market trends, strengthening qualifications systems and promoting the recognition of skills acquired through different learning experiences.
Second, the project will support capacity development and technical assistance to strengthen national institutions and systems. UNESCO will assist countries in improving governance arrangements, developing and implementing policies, modernizing curricula and qualifications, strengthening teacher and trainer capacities, promoting innovative approaches to teaching and learning, and enhancing systems that facilitate access to learning opportunities throughout life. Support will also be provided to strengthen pathways between formal, non-formal and workplace learning, helping learners move more easily between different forms of education and training and obtain recognition for their skills and competencies.
Third, the project will foster partnerships, policy dialogue and international cooperation to advance the global skills development agenda. UNESCO will mobilize networks of governments, development partners, private sector organizations, educational institutions and civil society to exchange knowledge, share promising practices and promote coordinated action. Through global and regional initiatives, conferences, communities of practice and collaborative platforms, the project will contribute to shaping international discussions on the future of skills, work and lifelong learning.
Expected deliverables include policy guidance, analytical reports, research publications, learning and assessment tools, capacity-building programmes, training resources, knowledge-sharing platforms and technical support for national reforms. The project will also contribute to strengthening data and evidence systems, enhancing policy dialogue, promoting innovative learning pathways and expanding opportunities for learners to develop skills throughout their lives.
Ultimately, the project seeks to help countries build more inclusive, adaptable and resilient lifelong learning systems that empower individuals, support sustainable and inclusive economic development, strengthen social cohesion and contribute to more equitable, peaceful and sustainable societies.
